title: survival dig states live: feet in water, ground column, sneak, air stand (16a.4 p.2/p.3b/p.4)
notes: A is teleported (RCON on vanilla, the client-side tp on ours) above each stand with pitch 90 and holds attack, so every dig goes straight down. water runs first: it absorbs the join/chunk-load burst of the run and its finish is trusted anyway (the digger's feet are in water), so a tick catch-up cannot turn it into a refused legitimate dig. It digs a dirt block under a one-deep walled pool at the feet (eyes dry) with a 25 s hold, because the client's in-water penalty may be 5x or 25x. ground/sneak dig a four-block column (grass, dirt, stone, leaves) in one 14 s hold: the bare-hand stone alone takes 7.5 s (150 ticks). air runs last with a 0 ms settle: the stand is 2.5 blocks above one isolated leaves block with bedrock below it, so a long hold cannot start a second, unintended dig. The aim check (raycast after the teleport) takes ~250 ms while the client's catch-up fall lasts ~50 ms of proxy time, so both attempts (settle 500 ms and 0 ms) began the dig while the player already stood on the block: the airborne state is unit-tested only, and a stand that presses attack before the aim check is still owed. Ours needs -HardnessReport (the timer) and -OursDevGeometry (the runner writes this command list there); vanilla builds the same list through the console. The artifact s12-samples.json carries A's player_action timings and B's stages/breaks/updates for the tick comparison. Submerged (eyes-in-water) digging stays a trace gap: its client time is 5-25x longer and does not fit one hold yet.
